newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 7.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Thursday:
- An Irish soldier who was kidnapped by the Hizbollah in June died last night in a helicopter crash during a training flight with the U.N. forces in south Lebanon.
- The government has been severely criticised by a U.N. agency for its crackdown on immigrants arriving illegally through the UK.
- Fianna Fail gained a seat as counting continued in the Senate elections last night and eight members were declared elected, seven of them outgoing senators.

- The first real engagement between the British government and Sinn Fein was how Gerry Adams described his initial face-to-face encounter at Stormont with the new Northern Secretary Mo Mowlam yesterday.
- SDLP insiders are predicting overwhelming support in party ranks for leader John Hume if he decides to allow his name to go forward for the Irish presidency.
- An Irish soldier who survived a kidnap ordeal at the hands of terrorists died in a helicopter crash in south Lebanon last night.
- A farmer was drowned after being forced to abandon his car in flood waters yesterday.
- Sterling nose-dived on currency markets yesterday leaving the Irish pound up a penny and a half at more than 89.5 pence.
- The war of words over the Hepatitis C scandal continued last night between Health Minister Brian Cowen and his predecessor Michael Noonan.

- Microsoft, the world's biggest software company, has agreed to invest $150 million in Apple stock and develop more programmes for its Macintosh computers in a crucial sign of support for the struggling computer maker.
